entities.summary: Lucius Domitius Alexander, a Roman emperor from 308 to 310 during the Tetrarchy, played a pivotal role in shaping the Western Roman Empire's decline. His vicariate of Africa and subsequent usurpation of the throne marked a turning point in the empire's fortunes. Alexander's reign was marked by internal power struggles, economic instability, and external pressures from the Sasanian Empire. Despite his efforts to maintain imperial stability, Alexander's reign ultimately contributed to the empire's fragmentation and the rise of new powers. The legacy of Domitius Alexander serves as a testament to the enduring complexities of the Roman Empire's final centuries.
